input.title: 3DCP Wall Buildability Assessment and Mix Design
input.markdown:
# 3DCP Wall Buildability Assessment and Mix Design

## Job
A 600 mm-high, 1.5 m-long straight wall with two filaments was assessed using a 25 mm nozzle, 50 mm/s print speed, and 60 min open time. Default geometry was 12.5 mm layer height and 29.61 mm layer width, giving 48 layers and a 60 s layer cycle. Default density was 2,100 kg/m³ and the safety factor was 1.5.

## Assessment of supplied material
Measured fresh properties were static yield stress 3.0 kPa and Athix 1.0 Pa/s. The physical verdict was **non-printable**, governed by elastic buckling. Buckling was predicted at layer 17 (212.5 mm). Plastic collapse was predicted at about layer 34 (approximately 423 mm, without the safety factor). The empirical collapse probability was 70.5%, used only as secondary evidence.

The current 60 s cycle would require approximately 7.825 kPa initial static yield stress or 2.675 Pa/s Athix. No schedule window was feasible: the required cycle was at least 160.5 s/layer, while the 60 min open time allowed at most 75 s/layer.

## Default 3DCP inverse design
The OPC-required default search evaluated 4,096 candidates and found no feasible mix. The best screening candidate was 100% Portland cement, w/b 0.335, and s/b 2.93. Its predicted initial static yield stress was 0.630 kPa [0.022, 10.908 kPa], with Athix 0.895 Pa/s. It remained non-printable, with predicted plastic collapse at layer 7 and buckling at layer 12.

The job requires approximately 10.705 kPa static yield stress at the end of the 48 min build. Because the rheology models are weak, candidate predictions are order-of-magnitude guidance.

## Published analogue
The database returned the CK0-C 3DCP mortar as an OPC analogue: 100% OPC, w/b 0.35, s/b 1.00, and PCE 0.25%. Its database-reported static yield stress at 48 min was 6.72 MPa; this unusually high value should be verified against the original paper.

## Conclusion
No defensible mix was identified for the unchanged job. Add filaments, brace or close the wall geometry, extend open time, or develop a faster-structuring mixture before experimental printing trials. Model results are correlations from published data and do not replace laboratory verification.

Literature analogue.note: Verify unusually high database-reported value against the source paper
